stemBlocks.value: The height h varies directly as the square root of the perimeter p. (a) Write an equation connecting h and p. (b) Given that h = 5.4 when p = 1.44, find h when p = 2.89.
Think first: Direct variation with a square root still follows the same pattern: one quantity equals a constant times the other.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p114-q01 from workbook page 114.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the variation statement as an equation with a constant k.
Substitute h = 5.4 and p = 1.44 to find k.

strategyBlocks.value: Write h = k√p, use the given pair to find k, then substitute p = 2.89 into the completed equation.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) h = k√p  (b) k = 4.5, so h = 4.5√p and h = 7.65 when p = 2.89

whyThisWorks.value: Direct variation means the ratio of h to √p never changes, so a single known pair fixes the constant k for every other pair. Once k is known the relationship is a complete formula, and any value of p can be converted to its h. Taking the square root first is essential — h is proportional to √p, not to p itself.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing h = kp and ignoring the square root.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing h = kp and ignoring the square root.

commonErrors.misconception: Substituting p = 2.89 without taking its square root.

examTip.value: Write the equation with k in it before you touch any numbers — it keeps the square root in the right place.
